Lessons.Title: Attributes of Other Quadrilaterals
ExplanationParagraphs: The first-edition 2021 Grade 3 Unit 7 Lesson 5 teacher lesson and preparation, all seven original student-task PDF pages, the six source figure SVG paths and dot-grid/summary figures were inspected on the authorized device. Student PDF SHA256: c7f21f414e4a857d806e13f6c3a302abde6f540a080106c5ec4bc13debf492f6. The original art is NOT embedded. The gated publisher Cool-down is unavailable; an independent Edulytics teacher-led exit task is not represented as its verbatim replacement.

Learning goals: identify every valid geometric class for a figure; draw quadrilaterals outside the square, rhombus and rectangle categories. Lesson sequence: 10-minute Number Talk, 20-minute All the Ways, 15-minute drawing task, 10-minute synthesis, 5-minute separately authored exit ticket. Original CCSS goals 3.G.A.1 and 3.OA.C.7. Offer rulers and partner discussion (MLR8) as in source.

Warm-up has four mentally computed division expressions: 70 ÷ 7 = 10, 77 ÷ 7 = 11, 63 ÷ 7 = 9, 56 ÷ 7 = 8. Derive 77 ÷ 7 by adding one group of 7 to 70, 63 ÷ 7 by subtracting one group, and 56 ÷ 7 by two fewer groups; do not treat this warm-up as optional geometry trivia.

Activity 1 has SIX source figures, each with a select-ALL category question. The original geometric SVG outlines were checked, not inferred from alt-text alone. Original figure 1 is an irregular quadrilateral (quadrilateral only); figure 2 is a triangle; figure 3 is a four-sided trapezoid (quadrilateral only); figure 4 has all four equal-length sides but not right angles (quadrilateral AND rhombus); figure 5 has four right angles but two different adjacent side lengths (quadrilateral AND rectangle); figure 6 is a ROTATED square and qualifies as quadrilateral, square, rhombus AND rectangle. These figures belong to the original publisher resource only; no copyrighted SVG paths or logos appear in Edulytics.

The precise rule is inclusion, NOT exclusive labels: square implies both rectangle and rhombus. Rhombus means four congruent sides with no right-angle requirement; rectangle means four right angles without equal adjacent side requirement; a quadrilateral is any polygon with four straight sides. The 2021 source also offers pupils a choice to discuss at least four of the six figures (accessibility) with MLR8 partner restatement; machine grading checks category names only, not mathematical justifications.

Activity 2 is four OPEN drawing tasks: construct a quadrilateral that is not a square, one that is not a rhombus, one that is not a rectangle, and several different quadrilaterals outside all three subclasses. Dot grid, actual side-length evidence and oral partner explanations remain teacher-reviewed. Valid first-party examples include a nonsquare 2×3 rectangle for the first, an unequal-sided 2×3 rectangle for the second, a non-rectangular slanted parallelogram for the third, and multiple trapezoids/irregular quadrilaterals for the fourth. A 2×3 rectangle CANNOT satisfy the third or fourth condition.

During synthesis, ask learners to explain why a square is inside multiple sets, why rotation does not change the properties, and which new quadrilateral constructions meet the exclusion rules. Original source section summary also distinguishes right triangles from other triangles and shows examples/nonexamples of rectangles, rhombuses and squares; these summary panels are reference only, not proof of an auto-graded drawing.

All source student figures and dot grids have been visually checked in the original seven-page PDF. Source-linked descriptions and answer sets are covered by source-to-first-party evidence. No publisher original Cool-down questions were accessed; Stage D build, authenticated grading, runtime test execution, CI and independent academic approval have NOT been performed.

KeyConcepts.Title: Quadrilateral
KeyConcepts.Definition: A polygon with exactly four straight sides.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Every rectangle, rhombus and square is a quadrilateral.

KeyConcepts.Title: Rectangle
KeyConcepts.Definition: A quadrilateral with four right angles.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Rotation does not change right angles.

KeyConcepts.Title: Rhombus
KeyConcepts.Definition: A quadrilateral with four equal-length sides.

KeyConcepts.Title: Square
KeyConcepts.Definition: A quadrilateral with four right angles and four equal sides.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Every square is both a rhombus and rectangle.
KeyConcepts.Example: Original figure 6 is a rotated square.

KeyConcepts.Title: Open construction
KeyConcepts.Definition: Many geometric answers are possible if their defining attributes satisfy the exclusions.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Teacher verifies side lengths, right angles, independence of examples and explanation.
KeyConcepts.Example: For not-square, a nonsquare rectangle is allowed, but not for not-rectangle.

WorkedExamples.Title: Number Talk relationships
WorkedExamples.Question: Use 70 ÷ 7 to find 77 ÷ 7 and 63 ÷ 7.
WorkedExamples.Method: One extra or one fewer group of seven.
Steps: 77 is seven more, so eleven groups.
63 is seven less, so nine groups.

WorkedExamples.Title: Select every valid name
WorkedExamples.Question: Which geometric category names fit the original sixth figure?
WorkedExamples.Method: Inspect equal side lengths and four right angles, not page orientation.
Steps: Its four right angles make rectangle.
Its four equal sides make rhombus.
WorkedExamples.Check: Order of labels does not matter, and selecting only square is incomplete.

WorkedExamples.Title: An open quadrilateral exclusion
WorkedExamples.Question: Construct a quadrilateral that is not a rectangle, rhombus or square.
WorkedExamples.Method: Create a four-sided trapezoid with unequal sides and non-right angles.
Steps: Make one pair of opposite sides parallel and of different lengths.
Avoid four right angles and four equal side lengths.
Label and justify the sides and angles for teacher review.
WorkedExamples.Check: No single scalar or picture hash can grade all valid drawings.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Select only square for a square.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The same shape also satisfies the rectangle, rhombus and quadrilateral definitions.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use inclusive category sets and select all correct names.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assume a rhombus has to appear as a diamond or all diamonds are squares.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Orientation does not define a shape; side lengths and angles do.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Verify each side and right angle independently.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Use a non-square rectangle for a not-rectangle drawing.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A non-square rectangle still has four right angles.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use a valid quadrilateral with at least one angle not equal to 90 degrees.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Turn four source drawing prompts into a single machine-graded number.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: There are infinitely many valid drawings and different explanations.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Collect drawing evidence and require independent teacher assessment.

SummaryPoints: All four source division facts are 10, 11, 9 and 8.
Source six classification sets respectively: quadrilateral; triangle; quadrilateral; quadrilateral+rhombus; quadrilateral+rectangle; quadrilateral+rectangle+rhombus+square.
Four distinct original drawing prompts stay teacher-reviewed.
No publisher images, source Cool-down or logo embedded; Stage D remains deferred.
